$comment: Declared skill-listing surface. Enforced by scripts/skill-surface.test.mjs, which runs
under `npm test`. Deliberately NOT enforced by hooks/pre-commit: that hook is not wired
into .git/hooks (issue #115), so a check placed there would never execute.
Why this file exists: plugin installs live in ~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json,
which is machine-local and has no repo representation. Without a committed declaration
there is nothing to diff and nothing to fail, so cleanup silently regresses. Changing the
surface means editing this file in the same commit -- a deliberate, reviewable act.
Claude Code loads every skill name+description into context. The budget is 1% of the
model context window; on overflow it drops descriptions starting with the LEAST-invoked
skills, so rarely-used skills lose their trigger keywords and become harder to invoke,
which keeps them at the front of the drop queue. Overlap evicts your own skills.
The target this file enforces toward is written up in docs/reference/skill-surface-standard.md.

plugins.$comment: Expected plugin -> install scope. Any drift in either direction fails the check.

expected.$stray-local-records: context7 and security-guidance were declared [local, user] until 2026-08-06. The local record was a duplicate enable in template-image-generator that registry.md had claimed was purged on 2026-06-18; it never was, and declaring the observed state as expected turned a known defect into policy. Removed via the casing fix below. They are NOT in the `removed` set -- the plugin itself is still wanted at user scope, and `removed` is keyed by plugin name, so listing one there would fail the resurrection check against its own legitimate install.
expected.$project-scoped: Scoped to another repo, so they never appear in user-level enabledPlugins and cost this repo nothing. marketing-skills moved user -> project on 2026-08-06: it was 47 skills and ~12006 always-on tokens in EVERY session, more than the entire ~10000-token listing budget on a 1M-context model and 74% of all plugin cost here. registry.md had claimed it was project-scoped since 2026-06-18 while it sat at user scope.

All 8 skills were read before grading on 2026-08-06: 2 dead (delegations already severed), 1 obsolete upstream (commands merged into skills), 3 inapplicable (they cover authoring a plugin; this repo authors none), 1 rejected (its gitignored .local.md config pattern conflicts with the committed project.json), and hook-development -- the only one with a live claim -- stale and WRONG: it says settings.json takes no `hooks` wrapper, which would produce a silently-ignored hooks block, and documents 9 of the platform's 31 events. Replaced by skills/creating-tools/hooks-reference.md, derived from the official docs and this repo's nine working hooks.

$casing-hazard: ROOT CAUSE of the repeated superpowers/feature-dev returns, diagnosed 2026-08-06.
`claude plugin uninstall --scope local|project` matches the stored `projectPath` against
`process.cwd()` with a CASE-SENSITIVE compare. Node reports `C:\Users\...` while older
records were written as `c:\Users\...`, so the lookup misses and the CLI reports the
plugin is 'not installed in local scope' -- from the correct directory. Fix: correct the
casing in the record, then let the CLI do the removal.
The same bug keys one directory as two projects: marketing-skills briefly had TWO project
records, written by the CLI itself 35 seconds apart, differing only in that first character.
Two earlier purges appeared to 'not stick'. They did stick -- installed_plugins.json has no
locking, every `claude` process holds a full copy, and a concurrent session writing it back
restored the deleted records. Not a daemon regenerating state; a lost update. Hand-edit only
with other sessions closed, and prefer the CLI.
CONFIRMED FIX, applied 2026-08-06 to context7 (local) and security-guidance (local): patch
the record's projectPath from `c:` to `C:`, THEN run `claude plugin uninstall X --scope
local` from the target repo. Both succeeded on the first attempt after the patch, having
failed repeatedly before it. Patch the casing at removal time, not before -- repointing a
live plugin's projectPath is only safe when the next step deletes the record anyway.
STILL LOWERCASE and deliberately untouched: frontend-design (project, klondike_gui). It is
legitimately project-scoped and wanted there, so it costs this repo nothing and needs no
removal. Patch it only if it ever has to come out.

$comment: Budget for this repo's own skills/*/SKILL.md descriptions (description + when_to_use).
perSkillMaxChars is the platform cap: a listing entry is truncated at 1536 chars
(code.claude.com/docs/en/skills), so anything longer loses its trailing trigger keywords.
totalDescriptionChars is a RATCHET, not a target. It sits just above the measured baseline
(12749 on 2026-08-06) so that unnoticed growth fails, while not manufacturing an immediate
trimming chore. The local surface is not what blew the budget -- one third-party plugin was
4.5x the entire local skill set. Trimming the long descriptions is worthwhile but separate;
lower this number when that work happens.
Resolution set and exemptions for scripts/reference-integrity.test.mjs.
Every entry is keyed by the thing being exempted and valued by the REASON it is
exempt. A missing or empty reason fails the schema check in skill-surface.test.mjs.
That requirement is the whole mechanism preventing this block from becoming the new
place dead references hide.
Resolution happens against COMMITTED STATE ONLY. CI runners are stock ubuntu/windows
images with no ~/.claude directory, so anything resolved by probing the local
filesystem is invisible to the gate that is supposed to enforce it. A machine-local
skill must be DECLARED here to be citable -- the same principle as plugins.expected.

localOnlySkills.pulser: Machine-local skill, not in this repo; cited by name in skills/adherence-audit/SKILL.md, which would otherwise fail its own audit.
localOnlySkills.write-article: Machine-local skill belonging to the content-engine repo; cited here but never resolvable from this checkout.

$comment: Namespaces that ARE component namespaces but are not covered by plugins.expected,
plugins.removed, or the local skill set. A `ns:name` pair counts as a CITATION only
if `ns` appears in the union of those four sets; anything else is prose that happens
to contain a colon (file:line, node:test, type:feat, justify-content:center).
This list is POSITIVE by design. The inverse -- 'ns is not a known skill or plugin,
therefore dead' -- is not provable: measured over this corpus it yields 48 findings
of which 17 are real. A positive declaration is diffable and cannot silently widen.
knownNamespaces.elements-of-style: Permanently declared dead. Never a local skill and never in plugins.expected or plugins.removed, so any `elements-of-style:` citation resolves to nothing. The one occurrence (skills/brainstorming/SKILL.md:295) is removed in the same slice that adds this entry; the entry STAYS afterwards as a recurrence guard, exactly as plugins.removed guards a deleted plugin. Do not delete it when the citation goes -- that would let the reference silently return.

platformAgentTypes.general-purpose: Platform-provided agent type, not a repo component. The correct subagent_type for the code-quality review lens.
platformAgentTypes.statusline-setup: Platform-provided agent type for status-line configuration.

historicalLedgers.plugins/registry.md: Removal ledger -- its purpose is to name removed plugins, so its citations must stay dead. Outside the slice-1 corpus (skills/, agents/, rules/); declared now because slice 3's corpus-wide entry point brings it into scope.
historicalLedgers.plugins/history.md: Append-only state-transition log; same reason as registry.md.

$comment: Declared exemptions for zero-inbound-edge nodes in the component graph.
A node with no inbound edge is either a defect -- something should cite it but doesn't --
or an entry point by design -- nothing is supposed to dispatch it. This block records the
latter. Every entry is keyed by the orphaned component and valued by the REASON it is
exempt. A missing or empty reason fails the schema check in skill-surface.test.mjs -- the
same mechanism that guards the references block above.
Checked in both directions by the graph invariant that consumes this block: every
zero-inbound-edge node must appear here, and every name declared here must still have
zero inbound edges -- a stale exemption fails exactly like a missing one.
